gatoh.agents.agents.Agent

class Agent(*args, **kwargs)[source]

A class to define the Agent objects that will interact with each other in an agent-based model.

Supported positional arguments:

  • <string> to set the Agent’s id.

  • <dict> of {hierarchy_name : weight} for the personal value that this Agent assigns to each social hierarchy

  • <float> in the range [-1, 1] to set the Agent’s initial opinion on the topic of interest

  • <bool> to define if the socially contagious belief will be of personal benefit to this Agent

  • <(string, float)> for the Agent’s defined personality and their social susceptibility (range [0, 1])

Any arbitrary keyword arguments that are passed to initialise this object will create a new attribute for the Agent object, and store the value of that attribute as the input data type.

If any pre-existing attributes are passed as keyword arguments, this simply sets the attributes to the input value.

If both a positional argument and a corresponding keyword argument are passed for the same attribute, the value given to the keyword argument will override whatever was passed as the positional value.

Parameters:

  • id (str, optional) – Positional argument – provides a unique identifier for an agent.

  • social_weightings (dict[str, float], optional) – Positional argument – <hierarchy : weighting> mapping indicating the personal value that the agent assigns to each social hierarchy.

  • opinion (float, optional) – Positional argument – the current opinion value that the agent is being initialised with.

  • personal_benefit (bool, optional) – Positional argument – a flag indicating if the socially contagious belief is of personal benefit to the agent.

  • behaviour_tuple (tuple[str, float], optional) – Positional_argument – a pair of variables detailing the agent’s defined personality and social susceptibility (range [0, 1]), respectively.

  • index (int, optional) – Keyword argument – the agent’s index within an AgentSet.

  • is_silenced (dict[str, bool], optional) – Keyword argument – <hierarchy : flag> mapping indicating in which social hierarchies the agent is silenced.

  • previous_opinion (float, optional) – Keyword argument – the opinion value held by the agent at the previous model iteration.

  • radicalised (bool, optional) – Keyword argument – a flag indicating if the agent is radicalised.

  • rw_distributions (dict[str, tuple[float, float]], optional) – Keyword argument – <hierarchy : random walk params> mapping for agent-specific dynamic hierarchy weightings.

  • opinion_rw (tuple[float, float], optional) – Keyword argument – (mean, variance) parameters for agent-specific stochastic opinion shifts.

Methods

__init__(*args, **kwargs)

add_attribute(name[, value, parameters, ...])

Dynamically add an attribute to this Agent object. If "value" is passed, an explicit initial value is given; if "mean" and "var" are passed, a value is generated from a random distribution. Supported random distributions are: - "gaussian" - "beta" - "gamma" - "uniform" - "levy".

change_opinion(opinion_delta)

A setter method that changes the Agent's current opinion by a given delta value.

change_opinion_rw(rw_params)

A setter method that changes the Agent's explicit opinion random walk parameters.

change_radicalisation(radicalisation)

A setter method that changes the Agent's radicalisation value.

change_rw_distribution(hierarchy, parameters)

A setter method that changes the Agent's explicit random walk parameters for a specific social hierarchy.

evolve_hierarchies(rw_distributions)

Experimental function that aims to model the constantly evolving 'intrinsic value' that Agents place on the social hierarchies that they belong in over time.

generate_agent(id, index, hierarchies[, ...])

Randomly generate an Agent object based on the input parameters.

get_attribute(name)

Return any existing or dynamically added attribute held by the Agent object.

life_events()

Experimental function that aims to model the ways in which Agent behaviours change according to major random life events over time

opinion_negation(hierarchy, ...)

Checks if the Agent has experienced sufficiently 'overwhelming' social pressure in a hierarchy leading to a complete reversal of their opinion.

opinion_silencing(hierarchy, ...[, ...])

Determines if an agent will become silenced in a given social hierarchy based on their attributes.

radicalisation(hierarchy_changes, ...)

Uses the agent's own opinion as well as the neighbours' opinions to determine if the agent has become radicalised in their actions.
